nodes.description: Public uint256 state variable holding the NFT supply cap (8888), read by claim().
Private mapping(uint256 => uint256) storing the timestamp written at mint time, used as the pseudo-random seed source for NFT traits.
Public minting entry point guarded by nonReentrant; computes tokenId from totalSupply()+1, writes block.timestamp into numbers and calls _safeMint to msg.sender.
Public view override that assembles the on-chain SVG/metadata, calling getBackGround, getFiveElements, getGossip, getTenDry, geTearthlyBranch and Base64.encode.
Internal view helper that reads numbers[tokenId] and derives a trait string via a keccak256-based random() seed.
Public view function reading numbers[tokenId] and computing a Color struct variant based on rand % 100.
Inherited ERC721 internal mint that transfers the token and invokes _checkOnERC721Received, performing an external callback to the recipient contract.
Caller-controlled address returned by _msgSender(); used as the mint recipient in claim and as the approval/ownership actor in ERC721 functions.
Miner-influenced block timestamp used in claim() as the stored pseudo-randomness source for token traits.
State write numbers[tokenId] = block.timestamp inside claim(); weak/timestamp-dependent randomness plus state mutation ordering relative to minting.
External call performed by _safeMint -> IERC721Receiver.onERC721Received on the recipient, executed before the minting state updates are finalized for the caller.
uint256 tokenId parameter of tokenURI(), forwarded to the trait getters and to toString().
Local uint256 tokenId in claim(), computed as totalSupply()+1 and used for the cap check, numbers write and mint.
Local string output in tokenURI() accumulating the encoded SVG and metadata before being returned.
Local Color struct info returned by getBackGround(tokenId) and consumed while building the parts array in tokenURI().

edges.reason: block.timestamp flows directly into the numbers mapping write inside claim(), making token traits depend on miner-influenced time.
The unsafe timestamp write persists into the numbers state variable that later seeds all trait randomness.
claim() executes the timestamp assignment to numbers as part of its minting logic.
msg.sender (via _msgSender()) is the caller of claim().
msg.sender is passed as the 'to' argument of _safeMint, which ultimately calls the recipient contract.
Local tokenId is passed as the minted token id into _safeMint.
Local tokenId is used as the mapping key in numbers[tokenId] = block.timestamp.
Local tokenId is compared against maxLimit in the require statement of claim().
claim() reads the maxLimit state variable to enforce the 8888 supply cap.
_safeMint performs an external call to IERC721Receiver.onERC721Received on the recipient, which can re-enter claim() (mitigated by the nonReentrant guard).
The tokenId parameter drives all lookups and string assembly inside tokenURI().
tokenId is forwarded from the trait getters into pluck() as the lookup key.
tokenURI() calls getBackGround(tokenId) and consumes the returned Color struct.
The Color struct returned by getBackGround is stored in the info local and its fields feed the parts array in tokenURI().
The output local accumulates the parts array concatenation and is the returned value of tokenURI().
tokenURI() indirectly reads numbers through getBackGround and the trait getters.
pluck() reads numbers[tokenId] to build the randomness seed for trait selection.
getBackGround() reads numbers[tokenId] to build the randomness seed for background selection.

normalization_plan.reason: tokenId is a parameter used only to index trait data inside tokenURI() and its getters, so it can be merged into the tokenURI function node.
Local tokenId in claim() is derived from totalSupply()+1 and used solely inside claim(), so it can be merged into the claim function node.
Local output in tokenURI() only accumulates the metadata string and is returned, so it can be merged into the tokenURI function node.
Local info holds the Color struct returned by getBackGround() and is consumed only inside tokenURI(), so it can be merged into the tokenURI function node.
